requirement:
The Rust outline profile under {cite}`requirements.references.outlines` MUST
identify items by segments describing their syntactic ancestry within the file,
such as `fn[run]`, `struct[Packet]`, and `mod[local]/fn[run]`, and MUST NOT
resolve Rust modules across files. Functions, methods, structs, enums, unions,
traits, impls, modules, macros, constants, statics, type aliases, and extern
blocks MUST be outline nodes. Impl segments MUST be named by their syntactic self
type and optional trait path, as `impl[Thing]` and `impl[Thing/Trait]`. `use`
declarations and other items without a suitable name MUST be anonymous. Selector
spelling MUST be documented.
rationale:
The implementation and documentation look sound. The tests leave one behaviour the requirement specifies without any coverage, so I'm judging this false.

**Implementation (in `src/outline/rust.rs`)**
- `KINDS` maps every item type the requirement lists to a node:
  - Functions, methods and trait method signatures: `fn`.
  - Structs, enums, unions, traits and modules: `struct`, `enum`, `union`, `trait`, `mod`.
  - Impls: `impl`.
  - Macros: `macro_definition` is named, and item-position `macro_invocation` is anonymous.
  - Constants, statics and type aliases (including associated types): `const`, `static`, `type`.
  - Extern blocks: `foreign_mod_item`, plus `extern_crate_declaration`.
  - `use` declarations: anonymous.
- `impl_name` builds `impl[Self]` or `impl[Self/Trait]` from the `type` and `trait` fields, as written in the source.
- `extern_name` uses the ABI string, or `Rust` when there is none.
- `item_macro` and `in_item_list` restrict anonymous macro nodes to item position.
- Only segments from the same file are produced, so modules are never resolved across files. `mod[external]` shows this.
- Selector spelling is documented in `md/reference.md`. The Selectors section covers the `kind[name]` format and percent-encoding. The Rust paragraph covers `impl<T> Trait for Wrapper<T>` becoming `impl[Wrapper<T>/Trait]`, and `use@…` and item-position macros being anonymous. The Outline profiles table lists the grammar node for every Rust kind.
- The `{impl}` markers cover the profile functions, `KINDS` and `PROFILE`.

**Tests (in `src/outline/tests.rs`)**
`rust_selectors_follow_syntactic_ancestry` and `selectors_name_syntactic_ancestry_and_duplicates` cover:
- nested modules and functions
- inherent and trait impls
- an impl on a non-path type (`impl [u8; 4]`, with percent-encoding)
- trait methods and associated types
- `extern "C"` and bare `extern`
- duplicate names (`#1` and `#2`)
- `macro_rules!`, union, enum, const, static, type alias and `extern crate`
- anonymous `use@` selectors, in `anonymous_selectors_use_identity_hashes` and the second test above

**Gaps**
- **Item-position macro invocations:** the requirement says macros MUST be outline nodes and unnamed items MUST be anonymous. No test has an item-position macro invocation such as `foo!{}` or `thread_local!{…}` at module level, and none asserts a `macro@<hash>` selector. My search for `macro@` and `macro_invocation` found nothing in tests.
- **Expression-position macros:** no test shows that they are excluded. `item_macro` and `in_item_list` are non-trivial logic with several branches, including the `expression_statement` wrapper case and `declaration_list`. All of it is untested.
- **Generic impls:** the documented `impl<T> Trait for Wrapper<T>` naming has no test. Only the `[u8; 4]` self type is exercised.

I found no `FIXME` acknowledging these gaps, so the result is false rather than FIXME.

text: :::{req} rust_item_selectors
The Rust outline profile under {cite}`requirements.references.outlines` MUST
identify items by segments describing their syntactic ancestry within the file,
such as `fn[run]`, `struct[Packet]`, and `mod[local]/fn[run]`, and MUST NOT
resolve Rust modules across files. Functions, methods, structs, enums, unions,
traits, impls, modules, macros, constants, statics, type aliases, and extern
blocks MUST be outline nodes. Impl segments MUST be named by their syntactic self
type and optional trait path, as `impl[Thing]` and `impl[Thing/Trait]`. `use`
declarations and other items without a suitable name MUST be anonymous. Selector
spelling MUST be documented.
:::{req} outlines
Habeas MUST parse Rust, Python, TypeScript, CSS, Markdown, TOML, and YAML
sources with pinned tree-sitter grammars, selected by file extension. Every
other text file MUST use a plain-text profile in which each line that is not
blank is an anonymous outline node of kind `line`. Each supported language MUST
have an outline profile that maps grammar node kinds to short outline kind names
and, for each mapped kind, states whether a node is named, and by which fields
or children, or anonymous. Only mapped kinds MUST appear in the outline; other
nodes MUST be transparent, so their outline descendants appear under the
nearest outline ancestor. A profile MAY attach grammar siblings to an outline
node, such as Rust attributes and doc comments preceding an item, so the outline
tree need not match the grammar tree exactly; attached siblings are part of that
node for its line range and hash. Every file's outline MUST have a root node
for the whole file, independent of language. Source in no other outline node,
such as top-level statements no profile maps, MUST belong to the root node;
profiles MUST NOT invent fallback kinds for it. Comments MUST NOT be outline nodes. Profiles MUST be
documented. Upgrading a grammar or profile MAY change outlines and MUST be
treated as a deliberate change.
